evidence.curator_note: SUBSTRATE READ FROM THE DRAWING (bottom of printed p. 218): a cycloalkane drawn as two horizontal rows joined by two diagonals - upper row '(CH2)m-CH-OCH3', lower row 'CH3O-CH-(CH2)n', with a diagonal from the left end of (CH2)m down to the lower CH and a diagonal from the upper CH down to the right end of (CH2)n. That is a ring CH(a)-(CH2)m-CH(b)-(CH2)n- back to CH(a), i.e. a cycloalkane carrying two methoxyl groups (map 2/3 on CH(a) = map 1, map 8/9 on CH(b) = map 7). A '+.' is printed on the OXYGEN of the upper OCH3 - n-ionization at that ether oxygen (mapped [O+:2]). The running text on the same page introduces it: 'In cycloalkanes with three or more methoxy groups, Equation 8.114 gives rise to a major peak in the spectrum' (methoxyl migration, Budzikiewicz et al. 1967; Winkler and Gruetzmacher 1970). NOTE the mismatch the book itself leaves: the prose says three or more methoxyls, the FIGURE draws two - this record encodes the FIGURE. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 2 arc(s), both above the upper row and both converging on the CH(a)-O bond, i.e. on the forming C=O+ pi bond: the right-hand arc starts at the '+.' odd electron on the oxygen and sweeps left-down; the left-hand arc starts on the (CH2)m-CH(a) bond and sweeps right-down. Both heads are single-barbed fishhooks. Moves <1,2> are those two drawn arcs; move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page) - it carries the second electron of the cleaving CH(a)-(CH2)m sigma bond onto the chain carbon (map 4), which is exactly what produces the radical dot the book itself prints on '.(CH2)m' in the intermediate. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the precursor SMILES puts charge AND odd electron on the ionized ether oxygen ([O+:2] with two bonds = one unpaired electron), matching the drawn '+.', so arc 1 has a real origin. INSTANTIATION (convention F): the scheme is generic in m and n; this record uses m = 3 and n = 1, i.e. 1,3-dimethoxycyclohexane (C8H16O2, M+. m/z 144.1145), a real compound of the drawn class. The step is the textbook radical-site alpha cleavage: the ring bond alpha to the charged oxygen breaks and the ring OPENS to the distonic ion the book draws next, .(CH2)m-CH(OCH3)-(CH2)n-CH=O+CH3.

Equation 8.114, SECOND arrow, labelled 're' (elimination). The book prints the intermediate on the left as the ring-opened distonic ion '.(CH2)m-CH(-OCH3)-(CH2)n-CH=+OCH3' (radical dot drawn on the (CH2)m terminus, '+' drawn on the oxocarbenium oxygen) and the single product on the right as 'CH3O-CH=+OCH3' labelled 'm/z 75'. This is the ABCD+ -> AD+ + BC elimination of Equation 8.106 with A = the migrating methoxyl (maps 8/9) and D = the oxocarbenium carbon (map 1): the C(b)-OCH3 bond and the C(a)-(CH2)n bond both break, the new C(a)-OCH3 bond forms, and a C=C forms between the two carbons that lost those groups. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 2 arc(s). Arc 1 starts on the vertical CH3O-C(b) bond, runs right and curls up, its head pointing up-right toward the 'C' of 'CH=+OCH3' - the methoxyl migrating with its bonding pair to the oxocarbenium carbon. Arc 2 starts on the diagonal (CH2)n-C(a) bond and sweeps down-left, its head pointing at the bond between 'C H' (= C(b)) and '(CH2)n' - that sigma pair becoming the new C=C pi bond. Moves <1,2> are those two drawn arcs; NO move is implicit - the two arcs account for all four bonds that change, and every species involved keeps its electron count (the (CH2)m radical is a spectator that is simply carried through). Both are transcribed as two-electron (heterolytic) moves: the migrating group moves as an intact substituent and both drawn products are correct closed-/odd-shell species under that reading. INSTANTIATION AND ITS ONE HONEST CAVEAT (convention F): with n = 1 (the value chosen here, m = 3, i.e. 1,3-dimethoxycyclohexane) the carbon that loses the methoxyl (map 7) and the carbon that loses the oxocarbenium fragment (map 10) are ADJACENT, so arc 2 forms a genuine C=C double bond exactly where its head points, and the neutral is the pent-4-enyl radical .CH2CH2CH2-CH=CH2 (C5H9, 69.0704). For n > 1 those two carbons are NOT adjacent and the same two drawn arcs would have to close a RING (a cycloalkane) instead of forming an alkene - the generic drawing does not resolve this, and the choice n = 1 is the curator's, made so that the encoded arrows produce precisely the drawn product. The ION is unaffected by m and n: CH3O-CH=O+CH3, C3H7O2+, the m/z 75 the book prints. RESONANCE (convention C): the dimethoxycarbenium ion is symmetric - CH3O-CH=O+CH3 and CH3O+=CH-OCH3 are equivalent resonance forms. The book draws the '+' on the RIGHT-HAND oxygen, i.e. on the oxygen that was already the oxocarbenium oxygen (map 2), and the migrated methoxyl as the neutral-drawn 'CH3O-'; the encoding uses exactly that form ([O+:2] double bonded, [O:8] single bonded).

NO MOD RULE IS CROSS-LINKED. rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no '8.114' key (chapter-8 rules stop at 8.14, German-edition numbering). Candidates were CHECKED with RDKit against this record's own instantiated species (convention E) and all fail. FOR THE ALPHA STEP the two ether alpha-cleavage rules have the RIGHT geometry but the WRONG substitution: (i) IMS_4_13_1 '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+.]8[C]9([H]10)([H]11)[C]12([H]13)([H]14)([H]15)>>[C.]1(...).[C]5([H]6)([H]7){=}[O+]8[C]9...' cleaves the C1-C5 bond while C5 forms the pi bond to the oxygen, so the cleaved bond IS incident to the pi-forming atom (correct, unlike the known chapter-4 geometry defects) - but it is diethyl-ether-specific: it demands CH3-CH2-O+.-CH2-CH3. SMARTS '[CH3]-[CH2]-[O+]-[CH2]-[CH3]' gives 0 matches on the molecular ion of 1,3-dimethoxycyclohexane. (ii) IMS_4_26_1 '[_A]1[C]2([H]3)([H]4)[O+.]5[_A]6>>[_A.]1.[C]2([H]3)([H]4){=}[O+]5[_A]6' is the generic version but still requires the alpha carbon to carry TWO hydrogens: SMARTS '[*]-[CH2]-[O+]-[*]' gives 0 matches, while the bare skeleton '[#6]-[#6]-[O+]-[#6]' matches 2x and '[CH1]-[O+]' matches 1x - so the H count on the ring METHINE alpha carbon is exactly and solely what fails. A ring-methine ether alpha cleavage is not encoded anywhere in the rule set, which is why polymethoxy cycloalkanes cannot produce this ion in the forward model. FOR THE 're' STEP nothing comes close: the only bond-forming (rd/substitution) rules are odd-electron radical-site displacements - 'substituion' [_A]1[C]2[C]3[_A+.]4>>[_A.]1.[C]2[C]3[_A+]4{-}2 needs a heteroatom that is both charged and radical, and SMARTS '[!#6;!#1]~[#6]~[#6]~[#7,#8,#16;+]' gives 0 matches on the distonic intermediate (whose charged oxygen has 0 radical electrons and whose radical carbon has 0 charge); IMS_4_43_rH '[#6]-[#6]-[#7+](-[#1])=[#6]' gives 0 matches (nitrogen rule). No rule in the set migrates an alkoxyl group to a carbenium centre. This equation is unmodelled by the MOD rule base.

evidence.curator_note: WHAT THE PAGE ACTUALLY PRINTS: the italic label 'm/z 75' directly under the product ion CH3O-CH=+OCH3, and, in the prose, that Equation 8.114 'gives rise to a major peak in the spectrum'. NO PERCENTAGE IS PRINTED anywhere for this equation, so relative_intensity is omitted (convention F) even though the ion is qualitatively called major; status is 'proposed' and detected=true, since the book does print an m/z for this ion. observed_mz 75.0441 is the monoisotopic, electron-mass-corrected value of C3H7O2+ computed by the curator for the nominal 75 the book prints - and it is INDEPENDENT of the generic m and n, unlike ms_context.precursor_mz 144.1145, which is the curator's instantiation (m = 3, n = 1, 1,3-dimethoxycyclohexane C8H16O2) and is NOT a number given by the book. The intermediate distonic ion has the same elemental composition as the molecular ion (144.1145) and gets no peak assignment: the page prints no m/z for it and it is not distinguishable by mass from M+.. MS CONTEXT (convention G): the page names no ionization energy, but the species undergoing the drawn reaction is the neutral molecule's odd-electron molecular ion (drawn '+.'), so the record uses the book's standard 70 eV EI context; no CAD/MI/CI experiment is named for this equation.
